proceedings.title: Regular bail
provisions: Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for matters before it

workflow.text: Analyse the FIR or complaint and chart the ingredients of each offence.
Record the arrest, remand and custody events and compute the custody period.
Draft the bail application from the record, with the grounds as proposals.
Review the draft against the conditions of bail and the record.

intakeQuestions: What is the FIR number, police station and the offences named?
When was the accused arrested, and what is the custody period?
What is the charge-sheet status?
Are there antecedents or a previous bail order?
What sureties can the accused offer?
evidence: The case diary, where the court has it

terms.meaning: Release of an accused person from custody while the case continues, with conditions.
The time from the arrest to the date of the application, computed from the custody record.
A person who undertakes to the court for the accused's appearance.

proceedings.title: Anticipatory bail
provisions: Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for matters before it

workflow.text: Analyse the FIR or complaint and chart the ingredients of each offence.
Draft the anticipatory bail application with the apprehension of arrest stated.
Review the draft against the record.

intakeQuestions: What is the FIR number and the offences named?
Has the applicant been called for interrogation?
Is there an apprehension of arrest?
What conditions can the applicant offer?
evidence: The notice or summons for interrogation

terms.meaning: A direction that a person not be arrested in a case, with conditions, before arrest.

proceedings.title: Quashing petition
provisions: Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for matters before it

workflow.text: Analyse the FIR or complaint and chart the ingredients of each offence.
Draft the quashing petition from the record, against the ingredient gaps.
Review the draft against the record and the ingredients chart.

intakeQuestions: What is the FIR number and the offences named?
Has the charge-sheet been filed?
Which ingredient of the offence is said to be absent?
Is there a private dispute the criminal case is said to dress up?
evidence: The documents said to be suppressed or misread

terms.meaning: The High Court's power to end a criminal proceeding that discloses no offence or is an abuse of the process.
One column per ingredient of the offence; each cell says what the record holds for it.

proceedings.title: Discharge application
provisions: Section 250 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for matters before it

workflow.text: Analyse the charge-sheet and chart the ingredients with the material for each.
Draft the discharge application from the chart.
Review the draft against the record.

intakeQuestions: Which offences does the charge-sheet name?
What material does the charge-sheet rely on for each ingredient?
Is any co-accused discharged?
evidence: The statements and documents relied on
The orders on co-accused, if any

terms.meaning: The court's finding that the material does not make out the offence, before the charge is framed.

proceedings.title: Criminal appeal
provisions: Section 415 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for matters before it

workflow.text: Analyse the judgment and its findings.
Draft the appeal and the suspension application.
Review the draft against the record.

intakeQuestions: What is the conviction and sentence?
Is the appellant in custody?
What is the date of the judgment?
Is a suspension of sentence sought?

terms.meaning: A prayer that the sentence not run while the appeal is heard.

proceedings.title: Trial
intakeQuestions: What is the charge, and which witnesses and exhibits does the record hold?

terms.meaning: The first information report of an offence.
The report the police file in court after the investigation.
The arrest, remand and custody events, each with its source.
